value.title: Servlet SSE under AsyncContext: bounded stream counter, dedicated executor and no async timeout

acceptanceCriteria.text: With `maxSseStreams(2)` and two open streams, a third request whose handler calls `res.sse()` receives `503` with the standard error body and its request id, because the adapter's counter throws a `503` `HttpException` before the exchange is marked started; after one stream ends a new `res.sse()` is accepted, and the counter is released also when the drain fails with `IOException` and when the exchange is aborted. [D-361; r3 W2-002]

The drain runs on a thread named `naruserve-servlet-sse-<n>` that is a daemon and not a container pool thread, the container request thread has returned from `service()` while the stream is open (a test records both thread ids and the return), and the executor never holds more than `maxSseStreams` threads. [D-361; D-106]

The servlet is registered with `asyncSupported=true`; a test filter in front of the servlet records, after the handler called `res.sse()`, that `request.getAsyncContext().getTimeout()` is `0` for every stream; and a stream kept open longer than the container's default async timeout (the test lowers it to 1 s) still receives a heartbeat after 2.5 s and is not ended by the container. [r4 W2-005]

An event sent from another thread after the handler returned reaches the client within 500 ms of the `send`, a `: ping` heartbeat reaches an idle client within `heartbeatInterval` plus 500 ms, and an event sent by the handler thread before the drain starts reaches the client while the handler still runs, each flushed without further writes behind it. [D-361; D-406; FR-SSE-002]

When the drain ends (client close, `close()` or the core's end report) `AsyncContext.complete()` is called, the stream's `onClose` listeners run once, and `abort()` on an SSE exchange also calls `AsyncContext.complete()`. [D-361; r5 W2-001] Abort, timeout or rejected drain submission before the SSE drain starts must still close the core client exactly once, free its registry entry and invoke close listeners.

A stream whose client closed its socket is detected by the next write or heartbeat failing with `IOException`, ends with the access-log cause `client` and returns its executor thread within two heartbeat intervals plus 1 s. [D-361; FR-SSE-004]

value.requirement: The system shall implement `HttpExchange.eventStream` on the Servlet adapter so that the exchange counts open streams against `maxSseStreams` (default 128) and answers `503` before the exchange is marked started when the bound is reached, otherwise calls `startAsync()` and `AsyncContext.setTimeout(0)`, commits status and headers, hands the container's output stream to `StreamDrain.attach`, runs the core drain loop on a dedicated bounded executor owned by the adapter — daemon threads named `naruserve-servlet-sse-<n>`, at most `maxSseStreams`, never the container's pool threads — returns at once so the container's request thread is released after the handler returned, and completes the `AsyncContext` when the drain ends.
value.rationale: Covers D-361, D-106 (the event-stream point), wave decisions SSE bound and thread owner on the Servlet adapter (r3 W2-002) and Servlet SSE registration (r4 W2-005: `asyncSupported=true` and `AsyncContext.setTimeout(0)` per stream), and I-012 and I-015. Measured: `spi/StreamDrain.java` is the core-owned drain loop type with `attach(OutputStream)`; FR-SSE-003 fixes the TinyHttpd mirror (counter that throws a `503` `HttpException` before the exchange is marked started, drain on the request worker). Decision: the Servlet counter is the adapter's own, with the same `maxSseStreams` of the frozen `ServerSettings`; the executor is created at `bind(ServerSettings, handler)`; heartbeat and event writes are flushed after each write so the container does not buffer them. Frozen: D-106 says the adapter chooses the thread that runs the loop ("an `AsyncContext` on the Servlet adapter"). Deviation (recorded): the loop runs on an adapter-owned executor thread, not on the container's request thread; a container pool thread blocked for the life of a stream would exhaust the pool, and the 128-thread bound keeps I-012 (no unbounded default). Deviation (recorded, inherited from FR-SSE-002 for D-406): sends made inside the handler before the drain starts are written directly on the handler thread, synchronised on the exchange, as on TinyHttpd. Pitfall: the default async timeout of a container (30 s on Jetty 9.4) would end a long stream with a `500`, hence `setTimeout(0)`. Pitfall: checking the counter after the exchange is marked started leaves the dispatcher unable to commit the `503` (r3 W2-001 of wave 7). Rejected alternative: running the drain on the container thread with a blocking loop; it holds one container thread per stream.
